entries.title: Jonah 2:1
segments: Affliction drives the erring child of God to earnest prayer and confession of sin.

entries.title: Jonah 2:2
segments:
vv 2-10. 
 
God can hear and answer prayer in the most desperate circumstances. The preservation of Jonah's life in the midst of deadly perils was infinitely easy to almighty power, and should encourage us to hope and pray for a full deliverance from our trials upon repentance and confession, even though they may have been brought upon us by our sins.

entries.title: Jonah 2:4
segments: Look again; seldom or never does a good man fall into absolute despair.

entries.title: Jonah 2:5
segments: Even to the soul; to the taking away of my life, which must have perished but for God's miraculous preservation of it.

entries.title: Jonah 2:6
segments:
For ever; this expresses his feeling as he fell into the abyss, and was swallowed up by the fish.  He considered himself as already in the lower world, whence there is no return. 
 
  Yet hast thou brought; here begins the language of confident faith; he speaks of his deliverance as already accomplished.

entries.title: Jonah 2:8
segments:
Lying vanities; all the vain confidences of those who forsake God, with allusion to his own conduct in fleeing from the Lord. 
 
  Forsake their own mercy; forsake God, the source of all mercy, and bring upon themselves his wrath.

entries.title: Jonah 2:9
segments:
But I; he speaks as one penitent and forgiven. 
 
  Will sacrifice; that is, when restored to the dry land.
